newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli Treasury offers plan to close budget gap.
newsitem.headline: Israeli Treasury offers plan to close budget gap.

text.p: Israeli Treasury officials said on Monday night that they would introduce two measures to cover a 350 million shekel shortfall in the 1997 budget.
The Treasury said it is planning to reduce a tax credit for working women, a measure that should raise 270 million shekels.
It also intends to force employers to partially finance workmen's compensation costs, which should raise another 80 million shekels.

The measures were announced a day after the parliamentary finance committee approved a package of tax rises to keep the 1997 budget within the targeted deficit ceiling of 2.8 percent of gross domestic product.
However, the Treasury said the new taxes had left a shortfall that should now be covered by the two measures.
